market_specific_notes: Philadelphia is a city where the metropolitan area crosses into two neighbouring states, and the federal locator searches by distance rather than by jurisdiction. That is usually helpful and occasionally confusing: the designation is federal, so an office over a state line is no less valid.

USCIS recognises all state and local health departments as civil surgeons for one specific purpose — completing “the vaccination assessments for refugees seeking adjustment of status”. In Philadelphia that body is the Philadelphia Department of Public Health. It covers vaccinations for that category, not the full examination for everyone.

USCIS also warns that “Many health insurance plans do not cover all portions of this examination.” Bring the card, then ask whether the practice accepts the plan for immigration medical examinations specifically.

Do not confuse the two places. The immigration medical examination is done by a civil surgeon in a private practice. The USCIS field office is where, in its own words, it holds “Interviews for all non-asylum cases (for example, getting a Green Card)” and “Naturalization ceremonies”. Philadelphia's is at 30 North 41st Street.

Philadelphia is carved out of the state immunisation registry, and this catches people out. Pennsylvania's PIERS public portal lets an adult, or a parent or guardian of a minor, print their own immunisation record — but providers in Philadelphia report to the city's own system, PhilaVax, not to PIERS. If you were vaccinated in the city, searching PIERS may return nothing even though the record exists.
Run the checklist below on a distance-based search rather than a state-based one. The designation is federal, so an office across a state line is no less valid.
local_vetting_points: Search uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon by ZIP code and let the radius, not the state line, decide the shortlist.
Confirm the practice appears in the federal locator under the name it bills and answers the phone under.
Ask whether tuberculosis testing is done on site and what a positive result does to the price and the timeline.
Ask what the office does when a vaccination record cannot be produced.
Ask who signs the completed form and how long after the visit.
typical_cost_ranges: There is no published figure. USCIS: “Fees for immigration medical examinations are established by the civil surgeon. Fees may vary by civil surgeon.”
USCIS advises calling several offices and warns the cost “can vary significantly”. A radius search that reaches into two neighbouring states usually widens the spread you will see.
Get the number broken into examination, tuberculosis and syphilis testing, missing vaccines, form completion and follow-up, so the offices you compare are describing the same work.
Filing Form I-693 costs $0; the published fee in the case is the I-485, at paper $1,440 or online $1,390 for an applicant over 14.
payment_options: USCIS tells applicants to confirm acceptable forms of payment with the office ahead of the visit.
Ask whether the quoted figure is payable in full on the day, and what a follow-up visit adds.
wait_time_notes: Ask how many visits the office expects in your situation, then ask how far you are willing to travel that many times.
Ask what the gap usually is between the examination and a completed, signed form when nothing is missing.
availability_notes: Confirm whether a same-week appointment refers to the examination or to the completed paperwork.
If a filing deadline is close, name the date on the call and ask the office to commit or decline.
named_resources_or_providers: USCIS Find a Civil Surgeon locator (official) — uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon
the Philadelphia Department of Public Health — phila.gov/departments/department-of-public-health. USCIS recognises local health departments as civil surgeons for the refugee vaccination assessment.
USCIS Philadelphia field office (PHI) — 30 North 41st Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104. From the USCIS field office ZIP data file at uscis.gov/about-us/find-a-uscis-office/field-offices.

Philadelphia Department of Public Health — phila.gov/departments/department-of-public-health. Philadelphia providers report immunisations to the city's own system, PhilaVax, rather than to the state registry.

Pennsylvania Immunization Electronic Registry System (PIERS) public portal — pa.gov/agencies/health/programs/immunizations/piers-public-portal. It states that the portal “allows individuals 18 or older and parents/legal guardians of minors under 18 to access, save, and print an official record of their immunizations that are documented within PIERS”.
USCIS Form I-693 page — uscis.gov/i-693, for the current form edition and filing instructions.
Listings are neutral examples and starting points for your own verification. Nothing here is a ranking or an endorsement.
city_intro_override: Philadelphia applicants often assume the civil surgeon must be in Pennsylvania. The designation is federal, and the USCIS locator searches outward from a ZIP code regardless of state line. Search by distance, verify designation in the tool, and then compare on price, language and turnaround.

primary_city_decision_block.title: Local civil surgeon comparison checklist
items: Verify designation in the official USCIS locator before comparing anything else.
Ask for the price broken into examination, labs, vaccines, form completion and follow-up.
Gather the vaccination records USCIS names before the first visit.
Ask what a positive tuberculosis test would do to the cost and the schedule.
Tell the office whether the I-485 is going by mail or online.
Confirm the form edition and the date the civil surgeon intends to sign.

heading: Philadelphia: the designation is federal, so search by distance rather than by state
i693_document_requirements: Form I-693 in the edition USCIS currently accepts.

Government-issued photo identification such as a valid passport or driver's licence. For an applicant aged 14 or younger, USCIS accepts identification showing name, date and place of birth and a parent's full name — a birth certificate with an English translation, or an affidavit.

A record of your vaccinations or immunisations, covering what USCIS names: DT, DTP, DTaP, Td, Tdap, OPV, IPV, MMR, Hib, Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, Varicella, Pneumococcal, Influenza, Rotavirus and Meningococcal disease.
Your health insurance card, with the coverage question already prepared.
Payment, in a form the office has told you it accepts.
vaccination_handling_notes: The records are the cheapest part of this process to get right and the most expensive to get wrong.

Work out first where you were vaccinated. Vaccinated elsewhere in Pennsylvania, the PIERS public portal is the route, and it says plainly who may use it: individuals 18 or older, and parents or legal guardians of minors under 18.

Vaccinated in Philadelphia, PIERS is the wrong place to look, because city providers report to PhilaVax instead. Start with the Philadelphia Department of Public Health, and give yourself time before the appointment.
Pennsylvania operates a statewide immunisation information system through which residents can request their own record; confirm with the clinic which format it will accept.
Refugees adjusting status may complete the vaccination assessment at a state or local health department under the USCIS blanket designation described above.
bilingual_support: The federal locator has a Languages Spoken filter covering a long list of named languages. It reflects what the practice told USCIS, not what its marketing says.
A language listed in the tool tells you it exists in the practice. Ask separately whether it covers the paperwork review, which is where a misunderstanding becomes a correction.
appointment_booking_notes: Decide before the exam how the I-485 is being filed. By mail the envelope stays sealed. Online, USCIS instructs you to open it and upload the form, then keep the original and the envelope until the case is decided.
Confirm the form edition and the intended signing date. Only the 01/20/25 edition is accepted for signatures dated 3 July 2025 or later.
Ask whether the slot you are offered is intake, examination, or the full path to a signed form.
Ask when the sealed packet is released and what the correction process is if an error appears on the form. Ask it before you choose an office an hour away, because a correction may mean going back.
